title: Person Registry
description: The artifact W9r emits (#550): one record per person, for a book translated for genealogy rather than for the translation. Validated by person_registry.py --build BEFORE it is written, so a malformed registry never reaches disk. It carries NO timestamp, deliberately -- a re-run over unchanged inputs is byte-identical, the same property the render/diff acceptance gate relies on elsewhere in this plugin. Everything a model asserted has either been checked against disk or affirmed by the independent adjudication pass; everything that was not is in refuted_claims[] or refusals[] with its reason, never silently absent. Numbers are never a model's: mention_count comes from the production occurrence engine, printed-form counts from the assembled target text.

verdicts_sha256.description: The digest of the Pass A verdict this registry was projected from. registry_claims.json carries it inside its own hashed body, and --build refuses when the verdict on disk has moved -- an affirmation is valid only for the exact claim it was shown.

assembly_currency.description: Stated rather than implied. --prep verifies that every manifest segment is converged, that its on-disk draft still hashes to the ledger's reviewed_draft_sha1, and that it appears in the assembled NodeStream -- which catches a partial assembly, a scope change and a post-assembly hand-edit. It does NOT catch a segment revised, re-reviewed and re-converged AFTER assembly ran: the new draft matches the new ledger and the old NodeStream still lists the segment. Binding that would mean persisting per-segment reviewed-draft hashes inside the NodeStream, i.e. editing assemble.py -- a PLUGIN_BUNDLE_MEMBER, whose bytes re-stale every converged segment of every project. Refused as disproportionate; run W9r immediately after W9 instead.

refusals.description: Units that reach no person record: refused by Pass A, or belonging to a person claim the adjudication pass would not affirm, or recorded by the project's own canon review_queue as unresolved.

refuted_claims.description: Every claim that did not survive into the artifact, kept with its reason. Two kinds: a claim the adjudication pass did not affirm, and a claim that fell with something it depended on -- a claim owned by a person whose identity was not affirmed (owner_identity_not_affirmed), or a relation whose TARGET person was not affirmed (relation_target_identity_not_affirmed), which the adjudicator may well have affirmed on its own terms. Nothing is silently deleted: a reader must be able to see what the registry declined to carry, not merely what it accepted.

person_id.description: The person the claim belonged to, or null for a non_person classification -- which belongs to a unit, not to a person.

shared_printed_forms.description: A printed surface more than one person claimed. It carries no count and no owner: attributing it to whichever candidate is more frequent is exactly the fabricated-person error this registry exists to avoid.

unattributed_units.description: Units whose occurrences the plugin refuses to attribute to anyone: a fold-key collision or an adjudicated homonym split reported by the occurrence engine, or a unit the engine never indexes at all (a senses-only form, a review_queue candidate).

excluded_by_canon_declaration.description: Canon entries the project itself declares are not identity-bearing (is_proper_name:false or basis:not_a_name). Listed rather than dropped, so the cast's denominator is visible.

canonical_target_form.description: Carried so the printed-name count can CONSUME this target's spans even though no person owns it: the renderer alternates over every canon entry and never branches on is_proper_name, so a declared-realia target still takes its span in the delivered text.

mention.description: One source-anchored occurrence, straight from the production occurrence engine -- so it does not depend on how that occurrence's translated surface happens to be spelled. This is the "reach the page" half of the record.

printed_forms.description: The target-language renderings as the book actually prints them, counted in the assembled target text by the plugin. `count` is null for every status other than "counted".

status.description: "boundary_ambiguous": the surface is printed in the book but has no countable span. Two things produce that -- the word-boundary rule refused every match, or a longer inventory form consumed them ("Marie" inside "JoAnn Marie", exactly as the renderer's own non-overlapping scan consumes it). The boundary case is itself the shared signature of a no-space script (a name followed immediately by a particle) and of an unrelated longer word containing the name, and nothing in the text distinguishes them -- so it is reported with the substring count rather than counted, dropped, or guessed at. substring_count is taken from the delivered corpus, never from the residue left after consumption: "not_found_in_target_text" is a claim about the book, and a reader draws "the book never prints this name" from it.

mention_count.description: Source-anchored occurrences across this person's attributable units. null when no unit is attributable -- an honest absence, never a zero, since zero would read as "not in the book".

evidence_truncated.description: True when at least one of this person's units had more occurrences than --max-contexts-per-form, so both LLM passes judged it on a bounded (evenly spread) view of the book rather than on every occurrence.
